newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap-Further downside seen on gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap-Further downside seen on gas oil.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady by midday on Thursday after bargain hunters appeared late on Wednesday, but brokers said the market was still under downward pressure as fundamantels remained weak.
The market lost more than $1.00 per barrel on Wednesday as sellers, led by a major, came out in force but the freefall was curbed late in the day when buyers emerged to bottom pick.
The prompt July swaps, which received the worst battering, was quiet on Thursday as sellers took a short breather with buyers bidding at $20.00 a barrel, unchanged from the previous day.

Brokers noted the widening contango as sellers offered at slightly higher levels for August and September, to be last quoted at $20.80/$21.05 and $21.85/$22.05, respectively, up from Wednesday's $20.80/$20.90 and $21.75/21.85.
Traders said the market would remain weak as long as China showed no buying interest for the third quarter despite current rock bottom prices, which had normally been a magnet for them.
China has decided not to issue import licences for the third quarter, Chinese sources said.

Traders now said that more refiners need to emulate Shell and Esso by cutting crude runs to help boost the gas oil market. The swaps jet fuel market was quiet with the jet/gas oil regrade steady at $1.80/$2.10 for July while August was slightly higher at $41.80/$2.00, from Wednesday's $1.70/$1./85.
Physical jet fuel was lower on Wednesday trading earlier at $22.10 per barrel and later at $21.85, both for July 24-28 liftings, free-on-board (fob) basis.
Fuel oil swaps rose along with the firm physical market which in turn has been receiving good buying support.
July was quoted at $99.25/$100.25, up from Wednesday's $98.50/$99.25.
August and September swaps were bid at $98.50 and was notionally offered at $99.50 from the previous day's $98.50/$99.25.
